text: At-most-once is fire and forget: a producer that doesn't retry, or a consumer that commits before processing finishes. An event is processed zero or one times — never more, but a failure at the wrong moment loses it entirely.

At-least-once flips the ordering: retry until acknowledged, commit only after processing succeeds. Nothing is silently lost anymore, but retries can create duplicates — the common default in real systems.

Exactly-once requires two real mechanisms: an idempotent producer, where the broker discards a retried duplicate using a producer ID and sequence number, and transactions that make a read-then-write pipeline atomic.

This is real, working exactly-once, not a marketing claim — but it adds coordination overhead, and it only covers the Kafka-to-Kafka hop. A write outside Kafka still needs its own idempotency handling.
At-most, at-least, and exactly-once — three real trade-offs, not one right answer. Next up: serialization formats, closing out Chapter 2.
